newsitem.title: USA: U.S. space shuttle heads home.
newsitem.headline: U.S. space shuttle heads home.

text.p: The U.S. space shuttle Columbia was homeward bound on Thursday after completing a 16-day science mission that was cut short in April.
Columbia, the oldest of NASA's four shuttles, was to touch down at Florida's Kennedy Space shortly after sunrise at 6:47 a.m. EDT (1047 GMT).
The shuttle fired its braking rockets at 5:44 a.m. EDT (0944 GMT), halfway around the world from the landing site, to begin a fiery hour-long descent through the atmosphere.

Weather conditions were favourable for the shuttle's homecoming, NASA mission control commentator Kyle Herring said. Rain showers in the vicinity of the shuttle landing strip had dissipated, and ground fog, which could have delayed the landing, never materialised.
Columbia's seven astronauts completed an $86 million research programme left unfinished in April, when the shuttle had to return to earth 12 days early because of a defective power generator.
It was the first time NASA had sent a shuttle and its crew back to space to complete a mission.
Since blasting off on July 1, Columbia's crew performed more than 30 experiments and ignited 206 controlled fires for combustion research, 42 more than originally planned.
